preconditions.description: The input is a single integer n representing the board size, where 3 ≤ n ≤ 100.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout.split()) == n and all(len(line) == n for line in stdout.split())
postconditions.description: The output consists of exactly n lines, each containing exactly n characters ('W' or 'B').

postconditions.expression: all(cell in ('W', 'B') for line in stdout.split() for cell in line)
postconditions.description: Each cell in the output grid contains either 'W' (white knight) or 'B' (black knight).

postconditions.expression: max_duels := sum(1 for (i1, j1), (i2, j2) in itertools.product(range(n), repeat=4) if (abs(i1 - i2) == 2 and abs(j1 - j2) == 1 or abs(i1 - i2) == 1 and abs(j1 - j2) == 2) and (stdout.split()[i1][j1] != stdout.split()[i2][j2]))
postconditions.description: The output grid maximizes the number of duels, where a duel is defined as a pair of knights of different colors that attack each other (i.e., satisfy the knight's movement rules).
